may_be_looking_for: Adults aged 18 to 80 years (with geriatric assessment needed for those 75 and older)
Diagnosis of a B-cell mediated autoimmune disease listed in the study (e.g., SLE, RA, MS, Myasthenia Gravis, etc.)
Have had an inadequate response to at least one conventional DMARD, one calcineurin inhibitor, and one biologic agent, or have a contraindication or toxicity to them
may_exclude_people_who: Are under 18 or over 80 without geriatric assessment
Have not tried or failed the required prior treatments (DMARD, calcineurin inhibitor, biologic)
Have other medical conditions that could interfere with the study (as determined by the study team)
patient_summary: This early-phase study is testing a new treatment called HBI0101 CART (chimeric antigen receptor T-cells) for people with B-cell mediated autoimmune rheumatic diseases. The main goal is to evaluate safety and find the highest dose that can be given safely.
patient_title: Study of HBI0101 CAR-T for Autoimmune Diseases
questions_to_ask_clinician: What are the potential risks and benefits of participating in this study?
How does HBI0101 CART work, and what side effects might occur?
What is the time commitment, including number of visits and follow-up?
source_grounding: Source Title: Phase 1 Study of HBI0101 CAR-T in Refractory B-Cell Autoimmune Diseases
Source Brief Summary: A Phase 1 study of HBI0101 BCMA-CART in B-Cell Mediated Autoimmune Rheumatic Diseases... evaluation of safety and identification of the maximum dose.
Source Eligibility Excerpt: Age 18-80, diagnosis of specific ARDs, failure to at least one conventional DMARD, one calcineurin inhibitor, and one biologic agent.
Source Conditions: List of 9 autoimmune diseases.
uncertainty_notes: The safety and efficacy of HBI0101 CART are not yet known. This is a dose-finding study, so the optimal dose has not been established.
Results from this early-phase study may not predict outcomes in later stages or in all patients.
what_researchers_are_studying: Researchers are studying HBI0101 CART, a type of cellular immunotherapy, to see if it is safe and what dose can be tolerated. The study is for patients with various autoimmune diseases such as lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, multiple sclerosis, and others.
